reason: A wipe of the system root is never a step in a task. If a path under / really has to go, name it.
The home directory holds the credentials, the keys and everything not in a repository. A task that needs to clear a directory can name that directory.
A download piped into a shell runs code nobody has read, from a host the fence may not even cover. Download it, read it, then run it.
A force push destroys work that is already pushed, including other people's. Push a new commit, or ask whoever owns the branch.
The same force push with the remote and branch named. Push a new commit, or ask whoever owns the branch.
Turning off the shell history hides what a session did from the person who has to review it. Nothing a harness does needs it off.
